This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
This is a military administrative and communications facility at White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico, completed in late 2023 to consolidate IT, networking, Land Mobile Radio control, and data processing functions previously distributed across older buildings. The 56,268 square foot, two-story building cost approximately 70.6 million dollars total, with 17.6 million in equipment, but the operator publishes no figure for IT load or rack capacity. Without a published megawatt specification, the facility cannot be ranked against commercial colocation or cloud infrastructure.

The facility was built to replace a 1962-era telephone and administrative network core building and to support range operations and testing at a major Army installation. It is not a leasable data center campus and does not offer third-party colocation. The absence of published capacity figures is consistent with a military internal-use facility rather than infrastructure that would be leased to external AI training operators.

New Mexico has fourteen mapped data center facilities on record but zero published megawatts of IT capacity across the state. This facility, though substantial in construction cost, does not change that figure because no IT load is disclosed. It cannot be evaluated as a constraint on AI scaling until or unless the operator publishes the megawatts dedicated to compute.
